tutorial.title: Discovering Child Elements
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how properties get transferred to different HTML elements through inheritance.

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent: We learned that HTML uses something called the box model. Thing is, everything in HTML is considered a box within another box.

lessons.title: Boxes inside boxes
lessons.interactiveContent:
When we add a <div> element around other elements, we put a bigger box around other boxes.

Make sure to pick <div>, followed by </div>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
When we add a <div> element around other elements, we put a bigger box around other boxes. Put Prince George's name inside one such box.

Make sure to pick <div>, followed by </div>.

lessons.title: Parent
lessons.interactiveContent:
Because the <div> element has another element nested inside it, we call it a parent element. The <p> element inside it is called a child element.

Make sure to pick <p>, followed by Prince George, and finally </p>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Because the <div> element has another element nested inside it, we call it a parent element.

The <p> element inside it is called a child element. Add the child paragraph that says Prince George inside the existing parent.

Make sure to pick <p>, followed by Prince George, and finally </p>.

lessons.title: Child
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we add another two paragraphs inside the <div> element, we have three child elements inside one parent element.

Make sure to pick <p> followed by </p> and then <p>, </p>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If we add another two paragraphs inside the <div> element, we have three child elements inside one parent element.

Make Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis sibling paragraphs inside the existing parent.

Make sure to pick <p>, followed by </p>, <p>, and finally </p>.

lessons.title: Non-transferable
lessons.interactiveContent:
When we style a parent element, there are some properties which only affect the parent, like border, padding, margin.

Let's give the <div> element a border.

Make sure to type border.

lessons.title: Transfer
lessons.interactiveContent:
But other properties, like color, are transferred to the child elements from their parent. Set color to brown.

Make sure to pick color followed by : and then brown, ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
But other properties, like color, are transferred to the child elements from their parent.

Make the text in the parent and all of its children brown.

Make sure to pick color, followed by :, brown, and finally ;.

lessons.title: Inheritance
lessons.interactiveContent:
When a child element receives a property from its parent, we call this inheritance.

Make sure to pick font-weight followed by : and then bold, ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
An element around another element is its parent. An element nested inside it is its child.

When a child element receives a property from its parent, we call this inheritance.

Text properties such as color and font-weight pass from a parent to its children.

Make the parent text bold so the child text inherits that style.

Make sure to pick font-weight, followed by :, bold, and finally ;.

lessons.title: No hard rule
lessons.interactiveContent: There's no hard rule for which properties are inherited. We'll learn more about how to look up which are inherited later.

lessons.title: Question: Boxes inside boxes
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we add a <div> element around other elements?

The div element acts as a box around the other elementsThe div element is another element in the code

The div element acts as a box around the other elements.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A <div> surrounds two paragraphs. What is its role on the webpage?

It acts as a box around both paragraphs.It turns both paragraphs into headings.It adds a border to each paragraph automatically.

It acts as a box around both paragraphs.

lessons.title: Question: Parent
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's an element surrounding another element called?

A parent elementA child element

A parent element.
lessons.hardModeContent:
In <div><p>Text</p></div>, what is the <div> element called?

A parent elementA child elementA paragraph element

Make sure to pick A parent element.

lessons.title: Question: Child
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's an element nested inside another element called?

A child elementA div element

A child element.
lessons.hardModeContent:
In <div><p>Text</p></div>, how is the <p> element related to the <div>?

It is a child element.It is a parent element.It is outside the div element.

It is a child element.

lessons.title: Question: Non-transferable
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we style a <div> element with a border?

Only the div element gets a borderThe child elements get a border as well

Only the div element gets a border.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A <div> contains three paragraphs and has a border. Which element gets the border?

Only the div elementEach paragraph and the div elementOnly the first paragraph

Make sure to pick Only the div element.

lessons.title: Question: Transfer
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we set a <div> element's color property to maroon?

The child element has color set to maroonThe child element has color set to black

The child element has color set to maroon.
lessons.hardModeContent:
In the displayed code, which text is shown in maroon?

Harry Potter & the Half-blood PrinceOnly the div element, not its textNo text, because color does not inherit

Harry Potter & the Half-blood Prince.

lessons.title: Question: Inheritance
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's inheritance?

When a child element inherits a property from its parentWhen a parent element inherits a property from its child

When a child element inherits a property from its parent.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A div has color: indigo and contains a paragraph. How does the paragraph get its text color?

It inherits indigo from its parent element.It passes its own color to the parent element.It gets a border instead of a color.

It inherits indigo from its parent element.

lessons.title: Example: Parent
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the tags so the <div> element is the parent and the <p> element is the child.

Make sure to pick <div> followed by <p> and then </p>, </div>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Make Jaden Smith a paragraph inside a div, so the div is the parent and the paragraph is the child.

Make sure to pick <div>, followed by <p>, </p>, and finally </div>.

lessons.title: Example: Child
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the tags so that the <div> element has two child elements nested inside of it.

Make sure to pick <p> followed by </p> and then <div>, </div>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Keep Siblings in its own paragraph. Then group Jake and Maggie as two child paragraphs inside one div.

Make sure to pick <p>, followed by </p>, <div>, and finally </div>.

lessons.title: Example: Non-transferable
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add a border around the paragraphs grouped inside the <div> element. The border should surround the elements as a whole.

Make sure to pick div.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A border stays on the parent element. Its children do not inherit separate borders.

Give the div around both paragraphs a 2px solid pink border. The border should surround the elements as a whole.

Make sure to pick div, followed by border, and finally 2px solid pink.

lessons.title: Example: Transfer
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add a property that child elements inherit.

Make sure to pick color: indigo;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Make both paragraphs inherit indigo text from their div parent.

Make sure to pick color, followed by :, indigo, and finally ;.

lessons.title: Example: Inheritance
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use inheritance to set the color for all the child elements nested inside the <div> element.

Make sure to type div.
